nodes.name: Admin
nodes.desc: Uploads batches of images and triggers exports of approved annotations. Role "admin" in the users table.

nodes.name: Annotator
nodes.desc: Claims a task, draws and labels bounding boxes on the image, submits it for review, and fixes rejected tasks.

nodes.name: Reviewer
nodes.desc: Works through the review queue and approves each submitted task or rejects it with a mandatory comment.

nodes.name: Image Annotation Tool
nodes.desc: Bounding-box annotation with a review step. Each uploaded image gets exactly one task; only approved tasks are exported as COCO-style JSON.
notes: Everything runs from one docker-compose.yml; there are no external systems. PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO come from public images.
Theoretical example project: a documentation fixture that has never been executed.

nodes.name: Web app
nodes.desc: React single-page app built with Vite and served by nginx. The same nginx proxies /api/ to the API container, so the browser only ever talks to one origin for API calls.
notes: Published on host port 3000 (container port 80).
Images, thumbnails and export files are NOT proxied: the browser fetches them straight from MinIO through presigned URLs.

nodes.name: API service
nodes.desc: Owns all business rules: login, image upload, task claiming, annotations, review decisions and export requests. The only writer of task status.
notes: Entry point: api/app/main.py registers six routers and seeds one demo user per role on startup (lifespan).
Published on host port 8000; OpenAPI docs at /docs. GET /api/health is the only route without auth besides login.
Only enqueues background jobs, by dotted path, so it never imports worker code.

nodes.name: Worker
nodes.desc: Background worker that consumes the "thumbnails" and "exports" queues from Redis and runs the matching job.
notes: Talks to PostgreSQL and MinIO directly through worker/clients.py; it never calls the API.
No retry or failure queue is configured in the code.

nodes.name: PostgreSQL
nodes.desc: System of record: users, images, tasks, annotations, reviews and exports.
notes: Schema is created by mounting db/migrations into /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d; there is no migration tool.
CHECK constraints repeat the allowed task statuses, review decisions and export statuses.
tasks.image_id is UNIQUE: exactly one task per image.

nodes.name: Redis
nodes.desc: Job queue between the API (producer) and the worker (consumer). Two RQ queues: "thumbnails" and "exports".

nodes.name: MinIO
nodes.desc: S3-compatible object storage with three buckets: original images, thumbnails and export files.
notes: Internal endpoint S3_ENDPOINT (http://minio:9000) for uploads; S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT (http://localhost:9000) is what presigned URLs are signed against.
Console on host port 9001.

nodes.name: minio-init
nodes.desc: One-shot container that creates the three buckets and exits. The API and the worker wait for it to complete successfully before starting.

nodes.name: App shell
nodes.desc: Shows the login form until a role is known, then mounts exactly one route for that role and redirects everything else to it.
notes: Role comes from localStorage, set at login; the API enforces roles independently.
Mounts AnnotatePage, ReviewQueuePage or AdminUploadPage at /annotate, /review or /admin. These render relationships are not drawn as arrows.

nodes.name: AnnotatePage
nodes.desc: Annotator view: works on one task at a time and lists the annotator's rejected tasks with the reviewer comment and a Fix button.
notes: Submit saves the boxes first, then submits, then claims the next task.

nodes.name: ReviewQueuePage
nodes.desc: Reviewer view: submitted tasks with thumbnails, the selected task read-only, and approve / reject buttons.
notes: Reject is disabled until a comment is typed; the API enforces the same rule.
Thumbnails in the queue list are loaded by the browser straight from MinIO through presigned URLs (not drawn as an arrow).

nodes.name: AdminUploadPage
nodes.desc: Admin view: uploads a named batch of JPEG/PNG files and starts a COCO export, polling until the worker has finished.
notes: Polls GET /exports/{id} every 2000 ms until status is done or failed.
The download link is a presigned MinIO URL, so the file is fetched from MinIO directly (not drawn as an arrow).

nodes.name: BoundingBoxCanvas
nodes.desc: Shows an image with its boxes. In edit mode dragging draws a new box and double-click removes one; without onChange it is read-only (review).
notes: Boxes are stored in original-image pixels; screen coordinates are divided by the display scale.
Boxes smaller than 2 px in either direction are discarded.

nodes.name: API client
nodes.desc: Thin typed wrapper around fetch for every API call. Keeps the JWT and the role in localStorage and adds the Authorization header.
notes: All calls go to the relative path /api, which nginx proxies to the API container.
claimNextTask() turns any failure (including 404 "no pending tasks") into null.

nodes.name: nginx
nodes.desc: Serves the built SPA with an index.html fallback for client-side routes and proxies /api/ to http://api:8000.
notes: client_max_body_size 200m, because image batches are uploaded through the API.

nodes.name: Auth
nodes.desc: Password login, HS256 bearer tokens and the role-check dependencies used by every router.
notes: Every router depends on it: Depends(require_role(...)) for role-restricted routes, Depends(get_current_user) for the rest. These cross-cutting dependencies are not drawn as arrows.
JWT_SECRET defaults to "change-me"; JWT_TTL_MINUTES defaults to 480.
Roles: admin, annotator, reviewer.

nodes.name: Images routes
nodes.desc: Batch upload for admins, plus the image serialiser that adds presigned URLs.
notes: Accepts image/jpeg and image/png only (415 otherwise).

nodes.name: Tasks routes
nodes.desc: Listing, claiming, submitting and reopening annotation tasks. Also holds the helpers the annotation and review routers reuse.
notes: require_assignee() (line 48): only the assigned annotator may change, submit or reopen a task (403).
get_task_or_404() (line 31) is shared with the annotations and reviews routers.

nodes.name: Annotations routes
nodes.desc: replace_annotations() swaps all boxes of a task in one PUT; list_annotations() reads them.
notes: Boxes are writable only while the task is in_progress (409 otherwise) and only by the assignee.
Validation: label non-empty, x and y >= 0, width and height > 0.
Reuses get_task_or_404(), require_assignee() and task_to_dict() from the tasks router.

nodes.name: Reviews routes
nodes.desc: The review queue and the endpoint that records a decision and moves the task to approved or rejected.

nodes.name: Export routes
nodes.desc: Lets an admin request a COCO export and poll its status. The file itself is built by the worker.

nodes.name: Task state machine
nodes.desc: The annotation task lifecycle: which action moves a task from which status to which, and which role may perform it. The statuses themselves are drawn in the Task lifecycle box beside it.
notes: Pure logic with no database or framework imports; unit-tested in api/tests/test_state_machine.py.
approved is the only terminal status (TERMINAL_STATUSES).

nodes.name: ORM models + session
nodes.desc: SQLAlchemy models User, Image, Task, Annotation, Review and Export, with the engine and the per-request session from api/app/db.py.
notes: The schema itself is owned by db/migrations/001_init.sql; the models only map it.
get_db() (api/app/db.py line 20) yields one session per request.
Route handlers use the Session directly; there is no repository layer.

nodes.name: Object storage client
nodes.desc: boto3 wrapper for MinIO. Uses two clients: an internal one for uploads and a public one for signing URLs the browser will fetch.

nodes.name: Job queue client
nodes.desc: RQ producer. Jobs are referenced by dotted path so the API does not import worker code.

nodes.name: Worker entrypoint
nodes.desc: Connects to Redis and runs an RQ Worker on the queues "thumbnails" and "exports".

nodes.name: Thumbnail job
nodes.desc: Reads the original image, records its width and height, and stores a JPEG thumbnail of at most 320 x 320.
notes: Thumbnail key is "<image_id>.jpg" in the thumbnails bucket, JPEG quality 85.
Until this job has run, images.width, height and thumbnail_key are NULL.

nodes.name: COCO export job
nodes.desc: Exports the annotations of all approved tasks as one COCO-style JSON file and tracks the run in the exports table.

nodes.name: login()
nodes.desc: Verifies email and password and returns an HS256 token carrying the user id and role, plus the role.

nodes.name: get_current_user()
nodes.desc: Decodes the bearer token and loads the user; 401 when the token is invalid or the user is unknown.

nodes.name: require_role()
nodes.desc: Builds a FastAPI dependency that returns the current user only if their role is one of the given roles.

nodes.name: seed_demo_users()
nodes.desc: Creates admin@, annotator@ and reviewer@example.com with password "demo" when the users table is empty. Called from the API lifespan hook.

nodes.name: upload_batch()
nodes.desc: For each file: stores it in MinIO, inserts the Image row and its pending Task. After the commit, queues one thumbnail job per image.
notes: Storage key: "<batch_name>/<uuid hex>-<filename>".
Objects are uploaded before the commit, so a failure mid-batch can leave objects without rows.

nodes.name: image_to_dict()
nodes.desc: Serialises an Image and adds presigned URLs for the original and, when it exists, the thumbnail.

nodes.name: claim_next_task()
nodes.desc: Returns the annotator's in_progress task if there is one; otherwise claims the oldest pending task and assigns it.
notes: Uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so two annotators never get the same task.
404 when no task is pending.

nodes.name: submit_task()
nodes.desc: Moves the assignee's task to submitted. 422 when the task has no annotations.

nodes.name: reopen_task()
nodes.desc: Takes a rejected task back into work for its assignee.

nodes.name: list_tasks()
nodes.desc: Lists tasks, optionally filtered by status and by "assigned to me". Any authenticated role may call it.

nodes.name: apply_action()
nodes.desc: The single place where task.status is changed. Asks the state machine for the next status and maps InvalidTransition to 409 and RoleNotAllowed to 403.

nodes.name: task_to_dict()
nodes.desc: Serialises a task with its image, its annotations and the most recent review decision and comment.

nodes.name: review_queue()
nodes.desc: Submitted tasks waiting for a decision, ordered by updated_at.

nodes.name: review_task()
nodes.desc: Applies APPROVE or REJECT to the task and inserts a Review row. 422 when rejecting without a comment.

nodes.name: request_export()
nodes.desc: Inserts an Export row with status queued, enqueues the export job and returns 202.

nodes.name: get_export()
nodes.desc: Returns the export status; download_url is set once the worker has stored the file.

nodes.name: export_to_dict()
nodes.desc: Serialises an Export and presigns a download URL when storage_key is set.

nodes.name: next_status()
nodes.desc: Returns the status a task moves to, or raises InvalidTransition (no such move) or RoleNotAllowed (wrong role).

nodes.name: TRANSITIONS
nodes.desc: Table mapping (current status, action) to (next status, role allowed to perform it). The five transitions drawn between the status boxes are exactly its entries.

nodes.name: allowed_actions()
nodes.desc: Lists the actions a role may perform on a task in a given status. Only used by the tests.

nodes.name: Task lifecycle
nodes.desc: The statuses a task moves through, from pending to approved, with rejected tasks going back to in_progress. Each arrow is labelled with the action and the role allowed to take it.

nodes.name: pending
nodes.desc: Initial status of every task, created together with its image at upload.

nodes.name: in_progress
nodes.desc: An annotator has claimed the task. The only status in which annotations can be changed.

nodes.name: submitted
nodes.desc: Waiting for a reviewer. Annotations are read-only.

nodes.name: approved
nodes.desc: Final status. Only approved tasks are included in COCO exports.

nodes.name: rejected
nodes.desc: A reviewer rejected the task with a comment. The assignee can reopen it.

nodes.name: upload_image()
nodes.desc: Stores the original image bytes in the images bucket through the internal endpoint.

nodes.name: presigned_url()
nodes.desc: Signs a GET URL against the public endpoint, valid for 3600 s by default. Returns None when the key is None.
notes: Signing is local computation; no request is sent to MinIO.

nodes.name: enqueue_thumbnail()
nodes.desc: Enqueues jobs.thumbnail.generate_thumbnail(image_id).

nodes.name: enqueue_export()
nodes.desc: Enqueues jobs.export_coco.export_approved(export_id) with a job timeout of 600 s.

nodes.name: export_approved()
nodes.desc: Marks the export running, builds the COCO document, stores it as "export-<id>.coco.json" and marks the export done; on any exception marks it failed and re-raises.
notes: task_count is the number of images in the export.

nodes.name: build_coco()
nodes.desc: Turns the query rows into COCO images, annotations (bbox, area) and categories. Category ids are assigned in order of first appearance of each label.

nodes.name: APPROVED_BOXES
nodes.desc: Joins tasks, images and annotations and keeps only tasks whose status is approved.

nodes.name: AnnotatePage
nodes.desc: Annotator view: works on one task at a time and lists the annotator's rejected tasks with the reviewer comment and a Fix button.
notes: Submit saves the boxes first, then submits, then claims the next task.

scenarios.name: Upload a batch + thumbnails
scenarios.desc: An admin uploads images. The API stores them and creates one pending task per image; thumbnails are produced afterwards by the worker. All /api calls pass through the nginx proxy.

scenarios.name: Annotate + submit
scenarios.desc: An annotator claims the oldest pending task, draws boxes and submits it. Status: pending → in_progress → submitted.

steps.label: no open task → oldest pending, SKIP LOCKED

scenarios.name: Review: reject, rework, approve
scenarios.desc: A reviewer rejects a submitted task with a comment, the annotator reopens and resubmits it, and the reviewer approves. Status: submitted → rejected → in_progress → submitted → approved.

scenarios.name: Export approved tasks (COCO)
scenarios.desc: An admin requests an export. The API only queues it; the worker builds the file and the page polls until a download URL appears.

scenarios.name: Annotate + submit
scenarios.desc: An annotator claims the oldest pending task, draws boxes and submits it. Status: pending → in_progress → submitted.
scenarios.goal: Get the next image annotated with labelled boxes and handed over for review.
scenarios.trigger: The annotator opens /annotate, which asks the API for the next task.
preconditions: Signed in with the annotator role: POST /api/tasks/next and POST /api/tasks/{id}/submit require it.
A task is pending, or the annotator already has one in progress; otherwise the API answers 404 "no pending tasks".
scenarios.outcome: The task is submitted with at least one box (an empty submit is refused with 422) and appears in the review queue.

scenarios.name: Export approved tasks (COCO)

scenarios.trigger: The admin clicks "Export approved annotations" on the admin page.
scenarios.preconditions: Signed in with the admin role: POST /api/exports and GET /api/exports/{id} require it.
scenarios.outcome: The worker writes exports/export-<id>.coco.json to MinIO and marks the export done with its task count; the page shows a presigned download URL.

versions.title: Add C4 model plugin: exploration, deck and architecture explorer skills
versions.message:
Add C4 model plugin: exploration, deck and architecture explorer skills

Three skills and one command that explore a codebase and generate a
reveal.js explainer deck and an interactive C4 architecture explorer
with JSON-LD and .rete export. Includes a theoretical image annotation
project as a test fixture, with the output generated for it, and
README screenshots taken from that output.

project.name: Image Annotation Tool
project.subtitle: examples/image-annotation-tool
project.title: Architecture map
project.intro: Humans draw labelled bounding boxes on images; every task is reviewed before it can be exported as COCO JSON. Start at the API service, then open "Task lifecycle" to see the statuses a task moves through. The Dynamic tab walks through upload, annotate, review and export.

versions.title: Ontology: publish the C4 architecture ontology, Turtle export, lossless RDF round trip
versions.message:
Ontology: publish the C4 architecture ontology, Turtle export, lossless RDF round trip

Add ontology/ with c4.ttl (the architecture: people, systems, containers,
data stores, components, code, relationships, scenarios and steps,
states and transitions, use cases), c4-view.ttl (how the explorer draws
it), c4-shapes.ttl (SHACL every exported graph meets), alignments.ttl,
a README, EXTENDING.md with good practices, and a worked deployment
extension. The namespace moves from urn:arch-explorer:vocab# to
https://caviri.github.io/c4-model-agentic-plugin/ontology/c4#.

The graph is now a complete description of every explorer diagram:
positions, view defaults, legend and level names are exported, and
archRdf.fromTriples rebuilds the model from N-Triples, Turtle or
JSON-LD. build-explorer.mjs can build a page from a graph alone, and
check-roundtrip.mjs proves the page and screenshots are identical.

Scenarios gain use-case fields (actor, goal, trigger, preconditions,
outcome), filled for two example scenarios from the code. Turtle is
offered in the export menu, the editor and every build. A model can
carry its own extension terms through an rdf hook. The docs site gains
an Ontology section with generated term pages and serves the .ttl files.

versions.title: Explorer: images on elements, colours per flow, compare roll-up, editor sidebar
versions.message:
Explorer: images on elements, colours per flow, compare roll-up, editor sidebar

Images: nodes, arrows, scenarios and steps can carry images
(screenshots, diagrams, photos, illustrations) with required alt text,
caption, credit and an illustrative flag. Boxes show a badge, the panel
a gallery, and a viewer opens them full size. Builds copy relative
images next to the page or embed them with --embed-images; the MCP
view draws only embedded ones and links the rest through the host.
Images are schema:ImageObject resources in the graph and round-trip.
The example gets three hand-made wireframes, labelled as illustrative
because the project was never run.

Flows: every scenario has a colour (set, or assigned from three new
tones per theme). The Dynamic view draws a flow in its colour, and a
flows overlay paints the arrows each flow travels on the map, with
numbered chips and a legend; shared arrows show stripes. show_flows is
a new page and MCP tool.

Compare mode tints added, removed and changed parts on the map in the
same colours as the change list, and rolls changes up: a closed box
shows +N -N ~N for everything inside it, merged arrows carry their
changes, and selecting a box lists the changes inside it.

Editor: edit mode gets a sidebar in place of the details panel, with
an Add palette grouped by C4 level to drag onto the map or into the
outline, an outline tree to filter, re-parent and reorder by drag,
and grouped properties including images and the flow colour. Every
action is undoable and works by mouse, touch and keyboard.
